steps.label: Two pain points · 1/7
steps.speakerNotes: SAM has two pain points. First, cost: SGD takes one gradient per step; SAM takes one to get the perturbation and a second at the perturbed point, so two forward and two backward passes. In the cost model SGD is 3 units and SAM 6, about twice.

steps.label: Two pain points · 1/7 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Second, scale: a ball of fixed radius treats every weight alike, so rescaling the weights changes the sharpness.

steps.label: Two pain points · 1/7 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Cost is reduced by computing less: SWP perturbs fewer weights, SDS handles fewer samples;

steps.label: Two pain points · 1/7 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: scale needs a change of the neighborhood's shape: ASAM.

steps.label: Two pain points · 1/7 (4)
steps.speakerNotes: for scale change the neighborhood shape: ASAM the three change different things: compute budget, sample selection, neighborhood geometry

steps.label: SWP · 2/7
steps.speakerNotes: SWP draws a mask each step, each component independently kept with probability beta, and takes the perturbation as the mask elementwise times the worst perturbation over beta. Weights not selected are unperturbed this step.

steps.label: SWP · 2/7 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: On the toy bowl the worst perturbation is 0.0981, 0.4903 and beta is 0.5; the four masks give zero, 0.1961 and 0, 0 and 0.9806, and 0.1961 and 0.9806.

steps.label: SWP · 2/7 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The mean of the four is exactly the worst perturbation, so the expectation matches; that is why we divide by beta, restoring what was dropped.

steps.label: Limits of SWP · 3/7
steps.speakerNotes: Do not over-read it; two limits. First, a single perturbation can exceed rho: the mask keeping both components has length 1.0, leaving the radius-0.5 ball.

steps.label: Limits of SWP · 3/7 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Second, what SAM uses is the gradient at the perturbed point, and the loss is not linear in the perturbation, so the expected gradient is not guaranteed unbiased.

steps.label: Limits of SWP · 3/7 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: How much time is saved depends on the implementation, not a fixed multiple of beta; no multiple is claimed.

steps.label: Limits of SWP · 3/7 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Whether the mask's noise acts like Dropout regularization has no evidence in the source and is not adopted here.

steps.label: Limits of SWP · 3/7 (4)
steps.speakerNotes: a Dropout-like regularizer? the source gives no evidence, so it is not adopted all we can say is that \mathbb{E}[\hat\epsilon]=\epsilon^{*}

steps.label: SDS · 4/7
steps.speakerNotes: SDS saves along the data dimension. First compute the perturbation on the whole batch,

steps.label: SDS · 4/7 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: then run a forward pass per sample to see how much the perturbation raises its loss.

steps.label: SDS · 4/7 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Only samples whose rise exceeds the threshold alpha take the second backward pass.

steps.label: SDS · 4/7 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: 3 rise >\alpha \mathcal{B}^{+} does the second backward pass

steps.label: SDS · 4/7 (4)
steps.speakerNotes: Count the cost honestly: the first backward on the whole batch and the forward at the perturbed point on the whole batch remain; only the second backward shrinks with the kept fraction. 4 plus 2 times the fraction units per step against SGD's 3, with floor four thirds.

steps.label: SDS · 4/7 (5)
steps.speakerNotes: One more caution: the second gradient is computed only on the selected samples, so it is no longer an unbiased estimate of the full-batch gradient.

steps.label: ASAM · 5/7
steps.speakerNotes: SAM's neighborhood is an isotropic ball treating every weight alike. ASAM uses a neighborhood normalized by the weight scale: large weights get large allowed perturbations and small ones small, so the ball becomes an ellipsoid.

steps.label: ASAM · 5/7 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: For p equal 2 the worst perturbation is rho times T squared times the gradient over the length of T times the gradient.

steps.label: ASAM · 5/7 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: A check: weights 1, minus 2, 0.5, gradient 0.3, 0.1, minus 0.8, rho 0.1, gamma 0.01 give 0.0560, 0.0739, minus 0.0381, with normalized length exactly 0.1.

steps.label: ASAM · 5/7 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: On the toy bowl SAM's perturbation is 0.98 percent and 24.5 percent of the weights, very large in y; ASAM gives 7.1 percent in both.

steps.label: ASAM · 5/7 (4)
steps.speakerNotes: toy bowl (10,2): perturbation relative to the weights SAM: (0.98\%,\ 24.5\%) ASAM: (7.1\%,\ 7.1\%)

steps.label: ASAM · 5/7 (5)
steps.speakerNotes: ASAM does not save compute: still two forward and two backward passes, about twice the cost.

steps.label: Scale invariance · 6/7
steps.speakerNotes: Sweeping the scaling a of the two-layer minima (a, 1 over a) from a quarter to 8, they are all the same function. SAM's fixed-radius sharpness is 2.069, 0.614, 0.346.

steps.label: Scale invariance · 6/7 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The same function's sharpness varies by over 23 times. ASAM asks T to be scale-invariant; for gamma above zero this is only approximate, so the source's claim that it always holds is not accurate.

steps.label: Three methods · 7/7
steps.speakerNotes: The three methods change different things.

steps.label: Three methods · 7/7 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: SWP changes the compute budget: each step perturbs a random part of the weights; the perturbation's expectation equals the worst perturbation and its variance grows.

steps.label: Three methods · 7/7 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: SDS changes sample selection: cost is 4 plus 2 times the fraction over 3 times SGD. ASAM changes the neighborhood geometry: cost unchanged, about twice, sharpness nearly invariant to positive scaling.

steps.label: Three methods · 7/7 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: ASAM neighborhood geometry: \|T_w^{-1}\epsilon\|\le\rho cost unchanged (about 2\times), sharpness nearly scale-invariant approximate for \gamma>0; \rho is not comparable with SAM's

steps.label: Three methods · 7/7 (4)
steps.speakerNotes: The three can be combined, but they solve different problems; do not confuse saving compute with changing the neighborhood.
